title: Trajectory detection crashes on valid JSON values that are not objects
reasoning: json.loads can return lists, strings, numbers, or None. Both detection and parsing immediately call .get without validating the result. Thus a JSONL file containing null or [] raises AttributeError during format detection instead of returning False or continuing to a valid initialization event. Parsing has the same issue, including assistant events whose message is null, and leaks AttributeError instead of a contextual ParseError.
reproduction: Pass a JSONL file containing null to can_parse or parse. Both raise AttributeError. An assistant event with message set to null also crashes parse.
recommendation: Validate decoded event and nested message types before accessing fields. During detection, skip incompatible records; during parsing, report invalid event shapes with line-numbered ParseError exceptions.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were supplied or linked. The excerpts show handling for invalid JSON syntax but no corresponding validation for valid JSON with incompatible shapes.
suggestedRegressionTest: Cover scalar, null, and array records, plus invalid nested assistant message shapes. Assert detection remains boolean and parsing either accepts supported shapes or raises a line-numbered ParseError.
